        "statement": "Let $U\\cong I\\times\\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and its SI conventions be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B:\\Omega\\times I\\to\\mathbb R^3$ be an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]] of class $C^k$ with $k\\ge1$. Define the **electromagnetic energy density** $u$ and the **energy flux density** (Poynting vector) $S$ by\n$$u(x,t):=\\frac{\\varepsilon_0\\lvert E(x,t)\\rvert^2}{2}+\\frac{\\lvert B(x,t)\\rvert^2}{2\\mu_0},\\qquad S(x,t):=\\frac{1}{\\mu_0}\\,E(x,t)\\times B(x,t),$$\nwhere $\\lvert E\\rvert^2=\\langle E,E\\rangle$ uses the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], $\\times$ is the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] in the frame basis, and $\\varepsilon_0=(\\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is the constant of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then $u:\\Omega\\times I\\to\\mathbb R$ and $S:\\Omega\\times I\\to\\mathbb R^3$ are of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] (they are polynomials in the components of $E,B$), with $u$ in $\\mathrm J\\,\\mathrm m^{-3}=\\mathrm{kg}\\,\\mathrm m^{-1}\\mathrm s^{-2}$ and $S$ in $\\mathrm W\\,\\mathrm m^{-2}=\\mathrm{kg}\\,\\mathrm s^{-3}$; at fixed $t\\in I$, $u(\\cdot,t):\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ is a real-valued function and $S(\\cdot,t):\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R^3$ a spatial vector field on $\\Omega$, read in $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$.\n(a) [Pointwise definition] The definitions use only the values of $E,B$ at the same point $(x,t)$; no derivative of the fields and no convention beyond the fixed laboratory frame is used. (b) [Products and singular support] If $E,B$ are only locally integrable (the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]), the products $E_iE_j$, $B_iB_j$ and the components of $E\\times B$ need not be locally integrable and no product of distributions is defined: the displayed formulas then define $u$ and $S$ pointwise almost everywhere, and the framework uses them only where the local integrability of the products, respectively of the component being integrated, is separately established. No value of $u$ or $S$ is assigned at a point of singular source support. (c) [Quadratic character] $u$ and $S$ are quadratic in the fields, so decompositions of the fields do not make $u$ or $S$ additive; cross terms generally contribute. (d) [Status] This item defines quantities only; the interpretation of $u$ and $S$ as an energy density and an energy flux is the content of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and no identification of $(u,S)$ with components of a covariant tensor is made here.",

        "statement": "Let $(A,V,\\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $c>0$, and let $n\\in V$ be future unit, $\\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\\perp$, rest projection $h(v)=v+\\eta(n,v)n$ and norm $|w|=\\sqrt{\\eta(w,w)}$ on $n^\\perp$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\\,(c).\n(a) For every $P$ in the future closed cone $\\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ define the observer energy of $P$ relative to $n$ by $E_n(P):=-c\\,\\eta(P,n)$, the observer spatial momentum by $q_n(P):=h(P)$, and, when $P$ is nonzero future causal, the invariant mass by $m(P):=\\sqrt{-\\eta(P,P)}/c$.         "statement": "Let $(A,V,\\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.\n(a) A collision datum is a triple $(p;(P_1,\\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\\dots,P'_K))$ consisting of an event $p\\in A$, a finite nonempty list of incoming vectors in $V$ and a finite nonempty list of outgoing vectors in $V$, with side totals $Q_{\\mathrm{in}}:=\\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ and $Q_{\\mathrm{out}}:=\\sum_{j=1}^KP'_j$ formed as in [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]; the datum conserves if $Q_{\\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\\mathrm{out}}$. Two-sided data may be compared only through these totals.\n(b) A leg $P$ is massive with mass $m>0$ if $P=mU$ for some future timelike $U$ with $\\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and null if $P$ is a nonzero future null vector. A datum is on-shell if every leg is massive with a recorded mass or null; a mass-specified datum records the mass $m>0$ of each massive leg or the value $0$ for each null leg. The mass sum of a side is the sum of the recorded positive masses of its massive legs; a side is massive-only if all its legs are massive.\n(c) A datum is causal if every leg lies in $\\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; two-leg if both sides have two legs; equal-mass if in addition both sides are two-leg and the recorded masses agree pair by pair.\n(d) The definition is purely mathematical: it neither asserts that any datum describes a physical process, nor that a conserving datum exists for a prescribed list of legs, nor any law of nature. (b) [Classification] (i) **Linear polarisation**: $\\dim_{\\mathbb R}\\operatorname{span}\\{a,d\\}\\le1$; when $\\dim\\operatorname{span}\\{a,d\\}=1$, the trace is a nontrivial segment in that span traversed twice per period; when $a=d=0$, the trace is the single point $\\{0\\}$ and the fields are the zero wave.         "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]. A declared detector-response integral may be used only when its declared model and integral suppliers establish a finite real value. An extended nonnegative integral with value $+\\infty$ is not a component of this real-valued comparison map or a recorded finite rate.
